text:
sara: FYI — noticed a repeating latency ripple on a small set of serving nodes starting ~03:45 UTC. 95th/99th jump every ~30s for ~10m. Looks tied to KV prefetch bursts. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/inflight/rdw-obs (graphs attached).

ken: pinging — any correlation with admission control logs or microbatch sizing?

devon: i see microbatch_size oscillating between 1 and 6 on those hosts, admission throttles spike concurrently. profiler shows kernel selector flipping to the fallback kernel right before the spike.

lia: logs from host-42: ``[03:45:12] admission: admit=1 qlen=2 microbatch=1
[03:45:12] kselector: chosen=fast_fused
[03:45:13] kselector: fallback=scalar_fp16 (slow path)
[03:45:13] kv-prefetch: miss=0.35 hit=0.65 prefetch_batch=64``

sara: interesting — fallback happens at ~same time as a prefetch burst. Could be memory pressure from prefetch evicting ephemeral KV entries causing kernel heuristics to change?

raman: i ran a heap profile on the node earlier — saw a spike in device-side memory usage when prefetch_batch > 48. Prefetcher uses temporary buffers for stride windows.

ken: hypothesis: prefetch hysteresis + multi-tenant prefetch waves temporarily change sequence length distribution seen by kernel selector, causing it to pick conservative kernels that increase per-token latency, which in turn shrinks microbatches, creating a positive feedback loop.

devon: reproduced locally with a synthetic load: two tenants, tenant A generates repeated short completions, tenant B triggers a KV prefetch scan every 30s. When both run kernel selector flips after about 6 cycles and tail latency spikes. Script: ``./perf-sim --tenants 2 --prefetch-interval 30s --kv-batch 64``

lia: can we get a quick mitigation? options: reduce prefetch batch size, add prefetch rate limiter, or make kernel selector consider recent pivoted seq-len distributions (not instantaneous).

ken: rolling a quick config change to cap prefetch_batch=32 on canary fleet now. will monitor.

oncall-bot: deploy started by ken at 04:12 UTC — patch: prefetch.batch_cap=32 (canary subset).

sara: also toggled kernel-selector to prefer stable kernels for 120s if it sees repeated fallbacks. Not ideal long-term but should damp oscillation.

raman: after canary change metrics look better — 95th/99th tail drops by ~40% and microbatch sizing stabilizes around 4. No obvious throughput loss.

devon: logged reproducer and added unit test to the kernel selector to prefer hysteresis windowing. Filed follow-ups: RDW-8472 (prefetch rate limiter), RDW-8473 (kernel-selector hysteresis), RDW-8474 (kv-prefetch memory accounting).

lia: summary for postmortem: small multi-tenant prefetch waves induced short-lived device memory pressure which changed kernel selection heuristics, causing fallback to slower kernels. That increased per-token time, which reduced microbatch sizes via admission control, amplifying latency spikes. Mitigations: cap prefetch batch, add selector hysteresis, fix prefetch memory accounting.

ken: can we schedule a short retro + owner assignment tomorrow? i'll volunteer to lead the follow-up for the canary rollout and perf tests.

sara: thanks everyone — great cross-team triage. :thumbsup:
